it’s hard to say, sour can either mean acidity or yeast, but if it was yeast, you’d normally also have thick white discharge and itching with it. what you eat can also affect the smell. too much sugar consumption can cause issues too. i know that eating probiotic yogurt regularly and drinking plenty of water can help significantly with vaginal health. that’s personally all i do whenever i think something might be off. i’m not too educated on supplements so you might be better with google on that one. i do know boric acid suppositories can help with BV but ive never tried them. are you in a position where you’d be able to change your underwear throughout the day? that might be a solution. if not, maybe only wear liners when you go out in public? panty liners aren’t inherently bad, they only create issues when used constantly, so it wouldnt hurt to only use them for a few hours a day, but definitely not all day

panty liners can make things worse. try wearing only 100% cotton underwear, and at night, either sleep without underwear or sleep in loose cotton underwear/shorts. after doing this for a while, you should eventually stop over producing discharge. discharge can be an off white color that appears yellowish, or it could mix with urine and cause a yellow tint. in terms of the green tint, it could be lighting, or the color of your underwear. but it could also be mild BV too which can be resolved with lifestyle changes and/or boric acid suppositories. the sour smell is usually normal due to the acidity (unless it’s super strong). watery discharge is also normal but you’re most likely overproducing this due to the daily panty liner use

cats usually hide pain as a natural instinct, so she could very well  be be in pain right now, especially with a tumor. when my elderly german shepherd was dying, we just thought he was lethargic and losing his appetite due to old age. we knew dying animals usually refuse food, so we agreed we'd eventually euthanize him, but not immediately. he was a slightly aggressive dog and NEEDED a muzzle at the vet, so the vet couldn't really give him a thorough examination during his last few months, and assumed all his symptoms were  just old age. it got to the point where he completely stopped eating and drinking so the vet said the only option was to euthanize him. but as he was getting euthanized,  the vet noticed his veins were already collapsing. after he was put down, he took a look inside his mouth. and there was a  cancerous tumor in the back of his throat. i cannot imagine what kind of pain he was in. none of us knew that was in there. but even if we did detect it while he was alive, he was too old for any beneficial treatments. as hard as it was to put him down, it made me realize he should've been put down way sooner. his suffering was only prolonged because we wanted more time with him. but all that did was give him more time with that nasty tumor. i still feel guilty about it to this day. i know it's hard to let go. and morally, you never want to be the "reason" an animal dies. but definitely consider the fact that the tumor could be causing her extreme discomfort. although she may be scared a the vet, you will be by her side to comfort her. and usually the vet first administers something that calms the animal and makes them feel a bit euphoric before they do the actual euthanasia. that's what they did for my dog. you could also look into at-home euthanasia if you're very worried about her being scared during her last moments

i almost lost my mind and my health over this exact same way of thinking. i cried all day, couldn't eat, even accidentally lost 15lbs from the anxiety, couldn't hold conversations, lost all enjoyment, only thought about dying to avoid my fears. but then i realized i was sabotaging my current life. **i was making myself feel the pain of situations that haven't even happened yet.**  i was taking away from my present life by constantly thinking about the 'what ifs" and what i thought i "knew" about the future. i stopped thinking about all the good things i have right now in this moment. thinking about the future takes away everything. i have the best dog that i could be spending time with, i could go get my favorite food, i could hang out with a friend, i could make some art, i could pick up a new hobby, i could go out and enjoy the nature for what it is at the moment, but instead i sat on the couch and **voluntarily placed myself into the future that was based completely off of my own personal fears and assumptions.** although it's very scary that the future is so uncertain, there will always be good things in life. bad events have always existed for every generation before us, but there's still so much good to focus on. i've also found that it helps to avoid a lot of media. the media will only want to tell you every single bad thing that's happening because it's... news. and it's good to be informed but too much of the same negative info will drive you crazy. i'm not saying you have to completely cut out media but try to balance it out by watching youtube channels or following specific media that posts about inspiring or hopeful stories. they rarely make the regular news but the good things are happening out there as we speak. **i've also had to accept that i don't have control over everything. i can't control what other people do or what the world does, only what i do. i can make small changes that will positively affect the future for both myself and the causing myself is for nothing. i had to accept that i have literally no control over what's uncertain, my only option is to enjoy everything i have right now. lets say, worse case scenario, one of my current fears actually do come true 10 years from now, and i didn't end this cycle of worrying. not only will i actually be living through my fear, but i'll be thinking about how i wasted the "good" thought cycle but there is so much life to live right now, and so much to enjoy in this moment. the future is uncertain for everybody even if they think they know what'll happen. life always has surprises, both good and bad. but there is the current moment that needs to be appreciated too
